actual_basic_readings.basic_text: After Ne4, Black's knight on e4 now targets White's knight on g3. After Ne4, Bxe4 is the stronger tested reply than Qe2. In the Ne4 line: The recorded continuation is Bxe4 fxe4. Bxe4 captures the black knight on e4. fxe4 recaptures the white bishop on e4. The exchange leaves Black's pawn on e4 blocking the line from Black's queen on e6 to White's pawn on e3. The advanced piece has gone, but the recapturing pawn keeps that pressure closed. In the Ne4 line: The recorded continuation is Qe2 Ncd6. Ncd6 moves the knight out of the attack from White's queen on e2. After Ncd6, Black's knight on d6 supports Black's knight on e4. The recorded continuation is Nd6 Qb1 Nde4 Nxe4 dxe4 Bf1 Nd5. Nxe4 captures the black knight on e4. dxe4 recaptures the white knight on e4. Nd6 keeps the choice of which knight to offer on e4. Here Nde4 uses the knight originally on c4, leaving the knight from f6 for Nd5. From d5 it attacks White's pawn on e3 and White's pawn on f4, restoring pressure despite the blocked line. The immediate Ne4 exchange gives up that piece and this way of continuing the pressure. The compared root choices are Nd6 and Ne4.
